description:
FILED s470bn (Opus, 2026-09-05) from the round-27 constants
(docs/plan-speed-and-ir-s470.md ÃÂ§A.4.1).

THE MEASUREMENT Ã¢ÂÂ one-line programs timed END TO END, best-of-5, nothing
subtracted (the constant IS what a user waits for):

  constant                              perl(s)    PCL(s)   PCL/perl
  startup (`print 1`)                    0.0016    0.169     105x
  `use Moo; print 1`        cache WARM    0.0081    3.50      431x
  `use JSON::PP; print 1`   cache WARM    0.0098    6.44      658x
  `use JSON::PP`            cache COLD      -      13.42     (warm run after: 6.63)
  `eval "1"; print 1`                     0.0020    0.292     142x

THE CAUSE is one defparameter in cl/pcl-runtime.lisp:
    (defparameter *pcl-cache-fasl* nil
      "Ã¢ÂÂ¦ defaults to NIL as a correctness workaround for the module
       compile-file+load DOUBLE-EXECUTION bug. Ã¢ÂÂ¦ Loading as source is
       single-pass and correct, at the cost of slower module loads.  The proper
       fix (keep FASL, eliminate double-exec) is option C/D in
       docs/module-double-exec-bug.md Ã¢ÂÂ DO NEXT SESSION.")   [session 251]

So the module cache stores `.lisp` TEXT and SBCL RECOMPILES it on every run.
That "next session" is long past and the cost had never been priced.  It is
3.5-6.4 s per run per module set, against a codegen worklist whose whole
round-27 harvest is tens of milliseconds: **everything else in the ranked table
is smaller than this one row**, and A.0's metric is PCL's ABSOLUTE seconds.

WHAT IT NEEDS FIRST is the correctness half, not the switch: with FASL caching
on, compile-file executes the module body once (running BEGIN-time guarded sub
redefinitions such as Sub::Defer's deferred constructors), then `load` re-runs
the plain `sub NAME` installs and CLOBBERS them Ã¢ÂÂ which broke Moo subclasses
(empty attrs) and any module using define-then-guarded-BEGIN-redefine
(Moose/Sub::Quote/Type::Tiny).  docs/module-double-exec-bug.md options C/D.

BAR when taken: the full sweep (module load is invisible to corpus-diff), the
CPAN board (this is exactly what it exercises), and these five constants
re-measured on a quiet box.  Ease L; impact WIDER than anything else measured.


=== DONE (s470bp, 2026-09-05) ===
SHIPPED as `9599ecb` + guard `ed17037`.  The double-execution bug is an ORDER,
not a count: *pcl-fasl-build*, bound around and only around the compile-file
that builds a module fasl, moves p-BEGIN to load time and p-sub's LAMBDA
INSTALL with it, keeps %p-reserve-sub-name (shadow+intern, which the READER
depends on) at compile time, discards p-CHECK, and leaves p-eval-always ALONE
-- suppressing it fails JSON::PP's compile with "Package Exporter does not
exist", because it is (p-use "Exporter") in the compile pass that creates the
package before the reader meets a symbol in it.  Option C of
docs/module-double-exec-bug.md done in the RUNTIME's macros, so the emission
does not change at all (corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 files).

A fasl is keyed additionally by *pcl-runtime-identity* -- a CONTENT hash of
cl/pcl-runtime.lisp plus the SBCL identity, computed from *load-truename* while
the runtime loads, so it is baked into the cached core and costs nothing per
run (9 ms in source mode).  Failure falls back to the text with a one-hour
.failed marker; an invalid-fasl is refused before any of its forms runs; every
other error propagates.

MEASURED, interleaved on one tree and one core (PCL_NO_FASL_CACHE=1 is exactly
the pre-#1188 path), best-of-4, startup 0.164 s as the control:
    use Carp; print 1              0.406 -> 0.216   1.88x
    use Scalar::Util qw(blessed)   0.337 -> 0.170   1.98x
    use Moo; print 1               1.127 -> 0.417   2.70x
    use JSON::PP; print 1          2.751 -> 1.432   1.92x
The GuardBoot repro prints REPLACED and the Moo subclass probe prints
`Dog name=B, breed=lab`.

THE ACCEPTANCE TARGET (JSON::PP under 0.5 s) IS NOT MET, and the reason is a
SECOND cache, not this one: with every module hot, PCL_FASL_DEBUG reads
`PP.pm -> FASL HIT (0.858s)` while its four dependencies take 1 ms each, and
sb-sprof attributes the frames under it to pcl:p-eval -- the ~20 string evals
JSON::PP runs at load to generate its property accessors, each a
`pl2cl --server` round trip plus an SBCL compile, EVERY RUN.  Filed as #1200
with the design and its five pre-checks.  #1202 records the same disease in the
EXTENSION load (`pack("N",1)` = 8.3 s), which the USER has parked with pack.

BARS RUN: gate 210 files / 7132 rows (only the 13 pclxs xs rows); corpus-diff
IDENTICAL over 111 with silent drops 5 unchanged; emission-ab 25 lib + 320 wide
files SAME / 0 DIFF / 0 RCDIFF; companion op/require.t + op/do.t + op/inccode.t
identical on BOTH paths and equal to baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv.
NOT RUN (machine shutdown): the FULL perl-tests sweep, which a cl/ change
requires -- the next session must run it before this is merged.
subject: MEASURED, and it is the biggest number in the yardstick: `use JSON::PP` costs 6.4 s WARM / 13.4 s cold, `use Moo` 3.5 s - because *pcl-cache-fasl* is nil and the module cache stores TEXT
